newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 29.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* National Semiconductor is planning to buy designer Cyrix for stock valued at $536.3 million.
* Lincoln National agreed to acquire Cigna's life-insurance and annuity business for $1.4 billion.
* British Telecom is expected to win federal regulatory approval for its purchase of MCI in the next few weeks.
* News Corp said it may face a Justice Department antitrust challenge of its plan to buy Heritage Media.
* IMC agreed to acquire Freeport-McMoRan Inc.
* Bond prices continued to rise amid expectations of more benign economic date.
* American Express said quarterly earnings rose 15 percent from a year ago.
* Donna Karan stepped down as CEO of her namesake firm.
* Westinghouse posted a quarter profit, beating analysts' expectations.
* Elaine Garzarelli is fueding with the publisher of the market strategist's investment newsletter and it appears they're heading for a break-up.
* Intel agreed to buy Chips and Technologies for $420 million.
* United Parcel Service is losing business and laying off workers as talks between the company and the Teamsters union nears a strike deadline.
* Thailand said it will negotiate with the IMF to obtain a standby credit line, reducing the risk of economic meltdown.
* Now that Congress and the White House have agreed on a new tax package, long term capital gains, which already get favorable tax treatment under current law, will fare even better.
